segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, so Quicklane is asking for the 18-month extension today if we can get it. They’re at 42 seats now, want to add 13 on March 1, and keep the support add-on. Renewal value is like $68,400 before the add-on discount.

segments.speaker: Colleague
segments.text: Okay, that’s the one with the invoice issue from December, right? They said PO has to match the legal name exactly.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Exactly. And this is where I’m losing my mind a little. To get them a clean proposal, I had to update the account name in the CRM, then type the same seat count and dates into the pricing sheet, then retype it into the quote form, then open the billing tool and enter the billing contact and PO notes again, then send the discount through deal desk with the same start date, end date, product lines, and totals. Deal desk kicked it back because the billing tool rounded the prorate two dollars different, so I had to go back through the whole thing. This was like three hours yesterday and another hour this morning for a pretty normal extension.

segments.speaker: Colleague
segments.text: Ugh, yeah. For the two-dollar variance, just put a note in the approval that billing is source of truth. Who’s approving, Maya?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Maya and legal, yeah. Discount is 8%, so not crazy. Legal only cares because they want net 30 to stay and no auto-renew language changed.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Their ops lead said Friday, February 16, because their finance batch closes Monday. If we miss it, go-live for the 13 extra users slips to April 1, and they were pretty clear that’s bad for their warehouse rollout.

segments.speaker: Colleague
segments.text: Okay. Send me the latest PDF and the approval note. I’ll sanity check the seat math and ping Maya if it’s still sitting after lunch.
